land.text: the Aures Mountains, which revolted against the Vandal king Huneric; 'the Aures kingdom was fully independent' by his death in 484

predecessors.note: The infobox also gives 429 for the 'separation from the Western Roman Empire'; Cliopatria's Vandal Kingdom row (443-533) reaches the Aures.

land.text: the Kahina's 'sovereign Berber state from the Aures Mountains to the oasis of Ghadames' (698-703)

successors.note: Dihya was killed near Bir al Kahina after the Battle of El Jem in 703.

capitals.name: Arris
capitals.note: 'Capital: Arris in the 400s-500s; Khenchela in the 600s-700s'; the page gives centuries, so 599 is a rounding; coordinates approximate (not in the gazetteer).

capitals.name: Khenchela
capitals.note: A footnote says it is unknown whether Khenchela was truly the capital; the page says it was Dihya's base of operations.

rulers.name: Masties
rulers.title: dux, then Imperator
rulers.note: 'c. 484 - c. 516'; an inscription of 516 says he had been dux for 67 years and Imperator for 10.

rulers.name: Iabdas
rulers.note: 'c. 516 - 548' in the infobox, 'c. 516 - 539' in the table; he fled to Mauretania after the defeat of 539.

rulers.name: Dihya (the Kahina)
rulers.title: queen
rulers.note: The Aures infobox and table give 'c. 668 - 703' (35 years); the Dihya page says she ruled 'for five years' (698-703). The ruler strip uses the Dihya page; the years between Iabdas and her are not listed on the Aures page.

correction.text: the Aures Mountains of north-eastern Algeria (Batna and Khenchela), 'including parts of Numidia'; Masties' realm centred on Arris

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; the two provinces of the Aures massif (20,000 km2) are my reading of 'Mainly the Aures Mountains of present-day northeastern Algeria'. The first revolt against Huneric is 484 (infobox).

correction.text: the Aures Mountains, re-established after the Battle of Cillium in 544

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The kingdom is out of the picture 539-543 ('the Byzantines held the region until 544') and gets no keyframe for those years. No page gives its extent after 544 or before the Kahina; the Aures core is held.

correction.text: 'a sovereign Berber state' from the Aures Mountains to the oasis of Ghadames, 'the uncontested ruler of the Maghreb, a region then known as Numidia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Numidia (164,000 km2) for 'the Maghreb, a region then known as Numidia' plus a southern corridor of Gafsa, Tozeur, Kebili and a 100 km circle at Ghadames for the line 'from the Aures to Ghadames'; my reading, the page names only the two ends.

ledger.note: 484: the Aures breaks from the Vandals. Infobox 'Revolt against Huneric: 484'; Berber revolts 'sparked partly by Huneric's attempt to convert the Moors to Arian Christianity'; Masties 'established the kingdom in the Aures'. The Mauro-Roman page: 'Huneric died in 484 AD, by which time the Aures kingdom was fully independent.'

region.text: the Aures Mountains, held by the Byzantines 539 to 544

ledger.note: 539: the Byzantines conquer the Aures. Infobox 'Byzantine conquest after the Aures campaign: 539'; 'The Byzantines held the region until 544'; Iabdas 'fled to Mauretania after defeat in 539'.

region.text: the Aures Mountains, recovered from the Byzantines

ledger.note: 544: the kingdom is re-established. Infobox 'Re-establishment of the kingdom after the Battle of Cillium: 544'; the page names the battle without describing it.

region.text: the Aures around Baghaya and the Meskiana Valley

ledger.note: 698: the Kahina meets Hasan at Meskiana. 'In 698' she demolished Baghaya and the armies met at the Battle of Meskiana; she 'defeated Hassan decisively'.

region.text: the Aures around Baghaya and the Meskiana Valley

ledger.note: 698: Hasan flees to Cyrenaica. After the defeat at Meskiana 'he fled Ifriqiya, remaining in Cyrenaica for five years'.

region.text: Numidia and the line from the Aures to Ghadames

ledger.note: 698: the Kahina rules from the Aures to Ghadames. 'For five years' she ruled 'a sovereign Berber state' from the Aures Mountains to the oasis of Ghadames (698-703), 'the uncontested ruler of the Maghreb, a region then known as Numidia'; the Battle of Carthage page notes Hassan faced 'five years worth of insurrection in what was Numidia'.

region.text: the Kahina's state, Numidia and the Aures to Ghadames

ledger.note: 703: the Kahina falls and the Aures is conquered. 'Dihya was killed in battle near Bir al Kahina, ending the kingdom'; the infobox gives 703 for the Muslim conquest of the Maghreb. The Dihya page puts the Battle of El Jem in Ramadan (September or October) 703 and Hassan's killing of her near the well Bir al-Kahina.

wars.name: Berber revolt against the Vandals
wars.outcome: Berbers fought the Vandals under Gunthamund and Thrasamund; the Aures kingdom was 'fully independent' by Huneric's death in 484. The page dates none of these wars.
wars.note: Cabaon of Tripolitania 'nearly destroyed a Vandal army sent against him' (undated).

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of the Aures (Solomon's campaigns)
wars.outcome: The Byzantines conquered the Aures in 539 and held it until 544, when the kingdom was re-established after the Battle of Cillium.
wars.note: The page dates only 539 and 544; Solomon's campaigns against 'Berber tribes in Byzacena' and the fortified posts he built are undated, and Iabdas's end is 539 (table) or 548 (infobox).

wars.name: Hasan ibn al-Nu'man's campaign against the Kahina
wars.outcome: After Carthage fell Hassan marched into the Aures; the Kahina razed Baghaya and defeated him at Meskiana in 698; he withdrew to Cyrenaica for five years.
wars.note: The Battle of Carthage page puts Hassan's advance into the Aures after 698; Dihya's rule is 698-703 on the Dihya page and 'c. 668-703' on the Aures page.

wars.name: Battle of El Jem and the end of the Kahina
wars.outcome: Dihya was defeated at El Jem in Ramadan 703 and killed near Bir al-Kahina in the Aures; her head was sent to Abd al-Malik at Damascus.
wars.note: Other sources place her death at Tabarka (Dihya page).

certainty.note: A mountain kingdom: no page gives a frontier. The 698-703 state 'from the Aures to Ghadames' is a line between two named places.

notes: Cliopatria has no Aures row. Start 484 is the infobox's 'Revolt against Huneric'; the infobox gives 429 for the separation from the Western Roman Empire. 539-543 is a break (Byzantine rule) entered as a loss and a gain, with no keyframe for those years. Conflicts between pages: Dihya reigns c. 668-703 on the Aures page and 698-703 on the Dihya page (the ledger uses 698); the Dihya page says most Berbers joined her 'in the 680s, after Kusaila was killed' while Altava and the Aures page date Kusaila's death to 690; Iabdas ends 539 or 548; the Dihya page puts her death at Bir al-Kahina or Tabarka. The extent of the state between 544 and 698 is not on any page and the 690-697 interval is not covered (the Altava dossier gives Kusaila's lost land to nobody). Whether the Kahina held Kairouan after Hasan fled Ifriqiya is not stated and not entered. Gazetteer names needed: 'Aures' (the Aurès massif, Batna and Khenchela provinces, c. 35.3 N 6.5 E), 'Arris' and 'Khenchela' as places. The 'mauro-roman-kingdom' counterpart used by kingdom-of-altava needs its own dossier.
